description:
This video was made possible thanks to everyone on the Simple History Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/simplehistory

The transcript explains the WWII “mystery powder” as crystallized sulfanilamide and sulfadiazine used alongside a compression bandage. Soldiers received single-use doses: the powder packet was emptied onto the wound, and tablets were taken as part of the plan to kill bacteria and prevent infection. It also notes limitations—sulfa powder disinfects the outside and doesn’t stop deep infection well, and sulfadiazine wasn’t used for abdominal wounds due to nausea and stomach cramps; by the end of the war it was phased out in favor of antibiotics like penicillin. What other WWII medical tools should we cover next?
